title: How would you estimate how many passengers use Heathrow on an average day?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many passengers fly from or to Heathrow on an average day?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A supply-side estimate: start from flights, not people. Then compare it with the real figure, which shows exactly which assumption was off. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many passengers fly from or to Heathrow on an average day?

The approach

Supply side: flights per day × seats per flight × share of seats filled.

Tip: Write each step with its unit, so you never lose track of whether you are counting people, homes or purchases.

Step by step

  1. Take-offs and landings per day: 1,300
  2. × 180 seats per flight
  3. × 80% seats filled

That gives about 187k passengers a day.

Does it make sense?

Long-haul jets carry far more than 180 people, so the true figure is likely higher. Say so as a caveat.

Real-world check

Heathrow handled about 84.5 million passengers in 2025, roughly 230,000 a day, from around 478,000 take-offs and landings (about 1,300 a day). So the flight count in the estimate is right, and the gap is seats per flight: long-haul jets carry far more than 180 people.

Source: Heathrow media centre: record year 2025.
